sources.entry: Juice - Enhanced battery information display. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/brianmichel/Juice) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Juice - Make your battery information a bit more interesting.

summary.one_liner: Juice is a macOS app that shows battery charge as a custom, user-defined scale of text labels instead of the standard battery indicator.
summary.what_it_does: Juice replaces the plain battery indicator with a custom measurement scale. It uses Apple's IOKit framework to read power source information and receive callbacks when those values change. Each scale is a plist file that maps charge ranges (detents, in 10% steps in the sample) to text strings chosen by the user. A default value is shown when the app cannot determine the power source state. Users can create a scale from the preferences UI, which generates a plist file to edit, then rescan scales to select one from a dropdown. Custom plist files can also be dropped into the app's Application Support folder. Per the README, scale values are strings only for now.
use_cases: Show battery level as custom text labels
Create a personal battery measurement scale
Replace the default macOS battery icon
Get battery state changes from IOKit
Customize battery status wording on a Mac
how_to_run: Compile the app through Xcode using the sources
Or download the latest released binary from the project's releases
Open Preferences and click "Add New Scale" to create a plist file
Edit the plist's default, detents and title values in a text editor and save
In Preferences, rescan for scales and pick the new scale from the dropdown
notable: Builds custom battery scales from plist files with detents mapped to text
Uses IOKit power source callbacks to update when battery values change
Preferences UI can generate a new scale file for editing
Custom scales can be dropped into the app's Application Support folder
caveats: Scale values are strings only, per the README
Custom scales require hand-editing plist XML
Installation requires Xcode to compile from source, or using a prebuilt binary
